The passage describes Brahman as containing "all works and desires and all perfumes and all tastes," and says "He enfolds the whole universe." This indicates Brahman is omnipresent and immanent in all things. The statement that "this is the Spirit that is in my heart" suggests an indwelling presence, but the broader description supports a universal, all-encompassing nature rather than being limited only to the hearts of the faithful.  

Final answer: (A)
